problem: Map-based VLN-CE agents such as CM2 and SASRA use semantic top-down maps built from segmentation outputs. These maps cover only a fixed set of classes (27) and cannot encode object attributes like color, texture or material. So instructions such as 'long wooden dining table' or 'red carpet' cannot be grounded when several same-class instances exist or when the object is out-of-vocabulary or misclassified. End-to-end RGB-D agents (Seq2Seq, CMA, LAW) must learn mapping, grounding and planning implicitly, which is hard.
motivation: VLN instructions refer to many objects, often by attributes. The authors' AMT study finds that 51% of instructions contain attribute-described objects, and 33% of those trajectories show instruction-object ambiguity. Latent features of a segmentation network are known to carry color, texture and part information. Instruction-path pairs implicitly indicate where the mentioned objects are, since they lie near the path. Together these allow a richer map to be learned without manual map annotation.
key_idea: Project frozen U-Net latent features (fine-grained) plus a hallucinated 27-class global semantic map into one egocentric multi-granularity map. Shape that map with a weakly-supervised auxiliary task that localizes instruction-relevant objects, using a soft ground-truth derived from each map cell's distance to the GT path. The localization heatmap then attends the map for a waypoint predictor.
insight: Both granularities are complementary. On R2R-CE val-unseen, SR by map type is: no map (end-to-end RGB-D) 26.5, fine-grained-only map 31.6, semantic-only map 33.3, multi-granularity map 38.9. The weak localization supervision is what makes the map discriminative. Removing it drops SR from 38.9 to 33.1 and localization IoU from 36.7% to 6.9%. A soft distance-based target (SR 38.9) beats a hard thresholded one (SR 35.2). Which features are projected matters: U-Net last-layer features, which mix low and high levels via skip connections, give SR 38.9 vs 32.1 for first-layer features and 33.3 for classification logits. Middle-layer features (9×9) fail to converge. Semantic hallucination beyond the FOV adds a smaller gain (37.3→38.9). DAgger is essential (24.6 without).
method: Fine-grained map: RGB goes through a U-Net segmentation model (pre-trained on MP3D RGB following CM2, frozen). Its last-layer 64-channel latent features are projected with depth into an egocentric top-down map (MapNet-style), 12 cm per cell, map size m=100.

Global semantic map via hallucination: 3 Conv-BN-ReLU layers plus a small U-Net (2 encoder / 2 decoder blocks) map the fine-grained map to a 27-class semantic map that also covers unobserved space. It is trained with pixel-wise cross-entropy against GT semantic maps from MP3D 3D annotations (loss l_s).
Multi-granularity map encoder: each map passes through a conv layer, the two are concatenated, and a further conv produces the multi-granularity map M (c channels).

Instruction-relevant object localization (weakly supervised): a GRU state encoder takes [M, ResNet18 RGB features, DD-PPO ResNet50 depth features]. Its state attends to BiLSTM instruction features (scaled dot-product) to give an attended instruction vector. The predicted heatmap is P̂ = Softmax((W_q ī)(W_k M)^T). The target is P = Softmax of the min-max normalized inverse distance from each map cell to the GT path, trained with a KL loss l_o.

Waypoint navigator: the map is averaged with weights P̂ to give attended map features. A second GRU (CMA-style) takes [attended map, attended instruction, s_t]. FC heads predict a waypoint (Δx, Δy) and a progress value, trained with MSE. The GT waypoint is where the shortest path to the GT path intersects a 3 m circle around the agent (following LAW).
Execution: a frozen DD-PPO point-goal policy converts the waypoint (updated every 3 steps) into FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 15° actions. The agent STOPs when predicted progress exceeds 0.8.

Training: total loss L = l_s + 10·l_o + 10·l_p + 10·l_w. Teacher forcing runs 30 epochs on EnvDrop-augmented data. DAgger follows for 10 iterations × 5000 trajectories (oracle probability 0.5^n), 4 epochs each. Adam at lr 2.5e-4, 2 V100 GPUs, about 3 days.

setting.backbone: Frozen U-Net segmentation encoder (MP3D-pretrained) + ImageNet ResNet18 RGB encoder + DD-PPO-pretrained ResNet50 depth encoder + BiLSTM instruction encoder + GRU/attention CMA-style policy trained from scratch; frozen DD-PPO local policy for low-level control
setting.training_data: R2R-CE train split (VLN-CE: 16,844 path-instruction pairs over 90 MP3D scenes across all splits) plus ~150k EnvDrop-augmented pairs. Teacher forcing then DAgger (10×5000 collected trajectories). GT global semantic maps from MP3D 3D semantic annotations are used as supervision for the hallucination loss. U-Net pre-trained separately on MP3D RGB for segmentation.
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB-D (224×224, 90° HFOV, no panorama); maps built by projecting features with depth
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints (Δx, Δy) every 3 steps, executed by frozen DD-PPO as low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN-LEFT/RIGHT 15° / STOP (stop when predicted progress > 0.8)
setting.privileged: None at test time. GT semantics and GT paths are used only as training supervision. Egocentric map registration presumably uses simulator agent pose; this is not discussed.

numbers_note: OS in the paper is mapped to OSR. RxR results are cross-dataset transfer (R2R-CE-trained model, no fine-tuning) on the English split only, and are compared only against LAW variants. The test-unseen leaderboard numbers are printed as integers. Ablation tables (map type, auxiliary task, feature layer, hallucination, DAgger) are R2R-CE val-unseen only and are not listed here as separate entries.
results: On R2R-CE with monocular RGB-D, WS-MGMap reaches SR 46.9 / SPL 43.4 on val-seen and SR 38.9 / SPL 34.3 on val-unseen. This beats the map-based CM2 (42.9/34.8 and 34.3/27.6) and the strongest end-to-end baseline LAW (40.0/37.0 and 35.0/31.0). On the test-unseen leaderboard it leads non-panoramic methods with SR 35 / SPL 28 vs CM2's 31/24. It even surpasses some panoramic methods (HPN+DN val-unseen SR 36.0) but trails CWP-CMA (41.0). Transferred zero-shot to RxR-CE English val-unseen, it gets SR 15.0 vs 10.0 for LAW pano.
limitations: The semantic hallucination loss requires GT 3D semantic annotations (MP3D) for training.
The 2D top-down egocentric map cannot handle multi-floor navigation.
No real-world evaluation; it also produces longer trajectories (TL ~10 m vs ~9 m for CMA/LAW).
